There are those who say that the legalization of all drugs (or in Colorado, pot) is a bold, dangerous, and all-too-liberal experiment.

I would say that since all drugs were legal and available up until the twentieth century, the prohibition of recreational drugs is the experiment. We have tens of thousands of years of recorded history in which drugs have been legal, and a few decades of prohibition. Those decades of prohibition have brought us crime, corruption, overdoses, and even the creation of worse drugs that can be easily manufactured with household ingredients. (Would meth be more popular than cocaine if coke was easy to synthesize?)

In Colorado, we legalized pot with basically no visible downsides. Portugal legalized the possession (though not distribution) of all drugs a while ago. Despite the economy being in the tank, the harm -- in terms of crime, public health, and economics -- of hard drugs has fallen dramatically.

While philosophically, I don't believe that government has a valid role to play in telling people what to do with their own bodies, there is also the practical argument that prohibition is a failed policy, and failed policies must be reversed. So far, the only countries that meaningfully enforce prohibition are states like Singapore, which I would accurately describe a police state. Between freedom and a police state, I'll take my freedom, even if it means my neighbor can get high in the privacy of his own home -- something that bothers me not in the slightest bit.

To me, it's a no-brainer. And I'm finding it increasingly hard to even entertain the idea that prohibition of any drug has ever benefited society in a single way.
I would not want to live in any time previous to the 20th century.

All human beings are equal. For me (a human) to tell you (also a human, who is equal to me) that you can't own something or ingest it into your own body if no one else is harmed, is the pinnacle of disrespect. You are an adult. You are responsible for your own actions. How dare I attempt to impose my will over you, my equal? You own yourself and no one else has any legitimate claim to that. Not me, not politicians, and not the police. Prohibition is a slap in the face to our fundamental right of self-ownership. I do support it with a couple limitations.

Mainly, I don't think that meth or heroin should be legal for just anyone to procure; I think prescriptions should be required for those. Heroin has some nasty side-effects, as does meth - I think heroin is worse because of its withdrawal symptoms being potentially lethal. However, most of the issues surrounding heroin overdoses involve impurities - if legally regulated like how the Swiss do it, I don't foresee heroin being that big of a problem.

That said. In terms of regular recreational drugs, like MDMA, LSD, Psilocybin Mushrooms, DMT, 2C-* series (and the DO* series), and generally all psychedelic tryptamines... all of those should be legal. They do not pose much harm to the individual, and far less harm to society. The active-dose/lethal-dose ratio is incredibly low. For instance, alcohol has roughly a 1:20 ratio; Amphetamine is roughly around 1:10; Nicotine varies with tolerance. But with LSD? 1:1000+ (LD50 still unknown). DMT? 1:100000 minimum. Weed? 1:Physically Impossible. The 2C-* and DO* series have a lower active-dose/lethal-dose ratio, but it still is beyond what people normally take. One example would be a person taking 500mg of 2C-B, when the normal dosage range is between 12-24mg, and surviving with no lasting side-effects from that experience. Another example would be MDMA, where the dose is about 100-150mg per unit, and people have survived dosages of over 500mg easily (though I wouldn't recommend anything past 250mg at once...200mg gave me quite a bit of nystagmus (eye-twitching).

If legally regulated in such a way to control purity, as well as have appropriate packaging indicating:

  • recommended dosage,

  • dosage per unit,

  • recommended route of administration,

  • duration of effects

  • potential adverse side-effects and incompatibilities (2C-T-7 is infamous for being a Monoamine Oxidase inhibitor, and thus could not be combined safely with many other compounds; SSRIs would also be lumped in with this caveat)

Other things and bits of information would be handed out in pamphlets along with purchase. I feel people should be knowledgeable about the products they are consuming. Often times people ask me "Is it a good idea to mix ______ with ______" and usually, the combinations aren't terrible ("is 2C-B good to mix with alcohol?" Yes, but be careful because you can get dehydrated. "Can I take MDMA and LSD together?" Yes. Have fun). But having a pamphlet that goes through various drugs and labels combinations as 'okay' in most situations, 'caution', or 'do not mix' would be enough for people to know what's what. Going against those recommendations would be at their own peril. Similarly, ideal environments and activities should be suggested in those pamphlets. It never outright says "DO DRUGS" but rather, it should say that if you choose to, here are some activities to try out.

And THAT is how drugs can be sensibly, safely legalized with minimal effects on society as a whole. By keeping the purity tightly regulated, the dosage within acceptable limits, and the public well-informed on what they are taking, it would cut-down on a lot of mishaps which occur.

Two last things: Diazepam helps dull or eliminate most ill-effects from psychedelics, and drug testing (for reasons other than reasonable suspicion) should be banned.

To insert the banner simply go to subverse settings on the bottom right of your subverse and paste the following code into the "CSS" box: 

#header {
 background: url( insert URL to picture here ) no-repeat scroll;
 background-position: 50% 20%;
 height: 278px;
}

 

I additionally wrote a few lines to make the banner be seen in it's full width on mobile devices too (So it doesn't get cut at the left and right and therefore cut some letters if there are any)

@media only screen and (max-width: 1200px){
 #header {
 background-size: 100% auto;
 max-height: 260px;
 }
}

@media only screen and (max-width: 1000px){
 #header {
 background-size: 100% auto;
 max-height: 230px;
 }
}

@media only screen and (max-width: 800px){
 #header {
 background-size: 100% auto;
 max-height: 205px;
 }
}

@media only screen and (max-width: 600px){
 #header {
 background-size: 100% auto;
 max-height: 180px;
 }
}

@media only screen and (max-width: 500px){
 #header {
 background-size: 100% auto;
 max-height: 150px;
 }
}

@media only screen and (max-width: 400px){
 #header {
 background-size: 100% auto;
 max-height: 140px;
 }
}

@media only screen and (max-width: 300px){
 #header {
 background-size: 100% auto;
 max-height: 124px;
 }
}
